tools.name: forecast
tools.description: Daily high/low for any place from every free forecast: median, spread, rain, current obs and active alerts, with credits and the page URL. line ≈321 tok, week ≈566, table ≈1,567, series ≈1,564. Keep the credits and link the page when you repeat numbers. size=runs: one place, each source's newest run

tools.name: places
tools.description: Find a place slug by name, City, ST, airport code or lat,lon; says full blend or grid only. A successful result also carries structuredContent: the format=json body (outputSchema).

tools.name: sources
tools.description: Open sources groundhog uses: licence, latest run, age, status. A successful result also carries structuredContent: the format=json body (outputSchema).

tools.name: markets
tools.description: Kalshi and Polymarket weather markets (high, low, rain) in a place: settlement station and rule, the value so far under that rule, forecast daily max/min (or rain) at the station, our value and the official result once settled. No prices: read them from the venue (each row's event and event_url). Ne

tools.name: receipts
tools.description: How often our settle value matched the venue's result, with every miss. No prices. A successful result also carries structuredContent: the format=json body (outputSchema).

tools.name: coverage
tools.description: Which Kalshi and Polymarket weather series groundhog tracks (key, family, kind, city, station, product), which it sees at the venue but does not support and why, and when each venue was last read. The REST body of /api/v1/markets/coverage. No prices. A successful result also carries structuredConten

tools.name: search
tools.description: Connector form of places, for clients that only call search and fetch: places by name, City, ST, airport code or lat,lon as {results: [{id, title, url, text}]}; pass an id to fetch. Otherwise prefer places, forecast or markets.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Connector form of forecast: the 7-day forecast of a place id from search as {id, title, text, url, metadata}. Otherwise prefer forecast, or markets for a market city. Keep the credits and link the url when you repeat numbers.

tools.name: history
tools.description: As-issued history for backtests (no look-ahead): kind=daily (every source's daily hi/lo/rain per run at a place), nbm (NBM text columns: TXN, XND, P12, Q12; view=day = the books' day view), obs (settlement truth: CLI, routine-METAR max/min) or markets (what the markets tool served, each change; asof

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, fetch · Public sink: forecast · Destructive: forecast, places, sources, markets, receipts, coverage, history.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, fetch · Public sink: forecast · Destructive: forecast, places, sources, markets, receipts, coverage, history

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "forecast" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
